content.text: Hello! Today, we will tackle the **Maximum Path Sum** problem. A path sum is the sum of the node values along any path connecting any two nodes in the tree. Because the tree can contain negative numbers, finding the maximum path sum requires a bit of clever recursive tracking. Let's see how!

For any node $X$, the maximum path sum that has $X$ as its highest point is:
**Path Sum = Value of X + max(0, Left Subtree Contribution) + max(0, Right Subtree Contribution)**
Why do we use `max(0, contribution)`? Because if a subtree contributes a negative sum, it is better to ignore it completely (treat it as 0) to maximize our sum!
